Programmable device controllers are increasingly becoming an essential part of advanced user workflows, including for agentic programming. Logitech is now officially bringing a compact solution to market that can be placed anywhere on a desk.

Logitech today launched the MX Keypad, an accessory priced at US$99.99, featuring nine customizable full-color LCD keys for quick command launches, macro execution, and AI tool access.

The MX Keypad is priced at half the cost of the Logitech MX Creative Console.

If this hardware looks familiar, there's a reason. Logitech's MX Creative Console pairs an LCD keypad with a separate dial controller (dialpad) for adjusting settings and performing actions in creative applications.

The MX Keypad retains only the keypad portion, omitting the additional controller, priced at half of the Creative Console's US$199.99.

This new product is primarily targeted at developers and AI workflows, but its customization features are not limited to coding.

The entire user experience can be customized through the Logi Options+ application.

Through the free Logi Options+ application, users can assign shortcuts, preset prompts, scripts, and macros to each key. The device features two page-switching buttons supporting up to 15 pages of settings, while application-aware functionality automatically switches profiles when you switch between different applications.

This means the same set of physical keys can perform different functions in VS Code, Slack, Chrome, or other applications. The Logi Marketplace offers various plugins, profiles, and icon packs, while the built-in icon editor lets users customize the appearance of each key.

You can use AI to create your own AI keyboard.

My initial hands-on test involved connecting the MX Keypad to a MacBook Air on my desk, then having Codex use its computer control capabilities to create custom keys in Logi Options+ based on my ChatGPT usage habits on the Mac.

Having an AI coding agent set up physical keys to operate AI is quite poetic, and clearly highlights this product's selling point: putting your frequently used prompts and actions onto dedicated, clearly-marked keys.

The MX Keypad is the result of a collaboration between Logitech and GitHub. The product features built-in GitHub Copilot integration for VS Code, and both new and existing users can redeem a 3-month free Copilot Pro+ subscription through Logi Options+.

The MX Keypad supports third-party community plugins.

Logitech also noted that community-developed plugins for Claude Code and OpenAI Codex provide agent status tracking and terminal control features. Developers who want to dig deeper can use the Logi Actions SDK, which supports C# and Node.js, to create their own custom plugins.

The MX Keypad connects via USB-C and requires macOS 13 or later, or Windows 10 or later. The device measures approximately 3.6 x 3.1 inches and weighs just 96 grams, so it won't take up much space next to a laptop or keyboard.

The MX Keypad goes on sale today (September 8) in Graphite and Pale Grey, priced at US$99.99.
